rationale: W0 for n-decane (a fuel of FLEX-2, PSI-68), one shot for this fuel and not zero-shot: no n-decane outcome was opened, but the law is the n-heptane law of flex_heptane.wsp5, whose numbers were typed after the n-heptane train partition. Not fully blind either: the repository's literature review quotes published aggregate rates of n-decane droplets on the ISS; the hot and cool levels here were worked from property tables first and compared afterwards (0.41 against 0.3-0.4 and 0.29 against 0.33 mm2/s), and the oxygen limit of the cool flame (0.03 atm) is typed under the bound those published cool flames set. Each fuel-specific number is the n-heptane number times a ratio worked by hand from property values: the hot-flame level, its oxygen and pressure dependence and the heat-up from a transfer number that includes the heating of the liquid; the critical diameter of radiative extinction as the inverse of the mass burning flux; the cool-flame rate from the wet-bulb transfer number under a 700 K flame and its end diameter from an equal residence time; the unlit droplet as self-cooling evaporation with property constants. The prefix is trusted more and every spread is wider than for n-heptane. Literal revision of the fuel's lineage root (the D^2-law reference of n-heptane, copied without change), not a root, because the author has seen other candidates; it writes every authored element, so nothing of the root survives. The parent id is a placeholder until the fuel is registered in droplet6.rs and the root is built: tools/wsp/reassemble.py then writes it. See docs/wsp/research/phys_droplet_fuels.md.
